failure_summary.description: Agents misinterpret truncated keyword-style questions by extracting related named entities instead of inferring the implied temporal query.

patch.reasoning: The failure stems from a lack of guidance on how to handle truncated questions that imply a temporal or categorical query. The new rule directs the agent to infer the missing question component and prioritize contextual markers (like dates/centuries) over associated entities when interrogatives are absent.

edits.content: - **Implicit Query Inference**: For truncated or fragmentary questions lacking explicit interrogatives (e.g., '[Entity] [Event]'), infer the missing component (typically time, place, or category). Prioritize extracting corresponding contextual markers (dates, centuries, locations) from the text rather than defaulting to associated named entities.
